title: Scaled dot-product attention
summary: One query attends to four keys and mixes four value vectors. The teaching kernel computes scaled scores, max-subtracted softmax weights, and the weighted value sum as visible intermediates.
example:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

query = torch.tensor([[[1, 0, 1, -1]]])
key = torch.eye(4).unsqueeze(0)
value = torch.eye(4).unsqueeze(0)
context = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(query, key, value)
limitations: Fixed fixture: one batch, one query, four keys, key/value width=4, default scale 1/√4, no mask, dropout, causal mode, or grouped heads.
The simulator kernel explicitly materializes score and weight buffers to teach the operation; PyTorch may fuse or dispatch to different backends.

tensors.name: value
tensors.description: Four value vectors, chosen as basis vectors to expose the weights.

tensors.name: weights
tensors.description: Stable softmax of the scaled scores.

tensors.name: context
tensors.description: Weighted sum of the value vectors.

stages.title: Scaled query-key scores
stages.summary: For every key, compute the four-term query/key dot product and scale by 1/√4 = 0.5.
stages.insight: Materializing four scores makes attention’s quadratic query-key step inspectable.

stages.title: Stable softmax
stages.summary: Subtract the maximum score before exponentiation, sum exponentials, and divide each by the common normalizer.
stages.formula: a[k] = exp(s[k] - max(s)) / Σj exp(s[j] - max(s))
stages.insight: Max subtraction preserves the softmax while reducing overflow risk.

stages.title: Mix values
stages.summary: Each context coordinate is the weighted sum of that coordinate across all four values.
stages.insight: With basis-vector values, context equals the attention-weight vector.

kernel.name: scaled_dot_product_attention
